what_happened: The operator started two jobs, 6239 and yz2d, at the same time. The disk allowance only fits about one job's build. Job yz2d failed before its checks because only 1.5 GB of disk was free. Job 6239's baseline test also failed. This cost one retry and about 40 minutes. Neither job's work was judged bad.
cause: Parallelism is decided from job dependencies alone. Neither the plan nor the job launcher knows how much disk a job's build needs or how much is free. The only disk guard runs per job, just before checks, so it cannot see other running jobs. Disk is a shared resource that Athena does not measure or reserve when it starts jobs together, so a failure shows up only after work is lost.
prevention: Add an admission check at job start. It compares free disk against the estimated build size of the new job plus all running jobs, using the measured size of earlier builds. If the total does not fit, the job waits for a running job to finish instead of starting. The plan's parallel groups should state this limit. Then a parallel group can never start more jobs than the disk holds.
proposed_request:
Make Athena start jobs in parallel only when the disk allows it. Outcome: when two or more jobs are ready to run together, Athena checks free disk against the measured build size of each running job plus the new one, and starts the new job only if it fits with a safety margin. If it does not fit, the job stays queued and starts when a running job finishes, with a clear message saying it is waiting for disk. Acceptance:
- A test with a fake disk-free value shows a second job is held when the combined need exceeds free space and started when it fits.
- A held job starts automatically after a running job ends and frees space.
- The plan output marks 'could run in parallel' groups as subject to the disk check.
- Existing single-job behavior and the per-job disk guard before checks are unchanged.
